beats.subline: Thursday, October 22, 2026 close — a sharp AI-spending selloff hit tech hardest while the Dow finished essentially flat and gainers actually outnumbered decliners market-wide.
beats.body: Weak reactions to Tesla's and Meta's earnings reignited worries about AI capital spending, driving the S&P 500 to its worst day since July and the Nasdaq to its worst since June even though most individual stocks actually rose; oil prices jumped on escalating Mideast tensions, adding to the cross-currents.

beats.headline: Trump accuses Iran of lying about tanker attacks to inflate oil prices before midterms
beats.body: President Trump said Iran fabricated Thursday's reports of seven tankers hit in the Strait of Hormuz to drive up oil prices ahead of the US midterms, after the claim sent Brent crude toward $114 a barrel; Trump said Washington has stopped negotiating with Tehran, while Iran's foreign minister said the strait will stay closed until the US accepts a seven-day deal.

beats.headline: China claims 'indisputable sovereignty' over Pratas Islands after coast guard standoff
beats.body: China's Taiwan Affairs Office said Beijing has indisputable sovereignty over the Pratas Islands and their adjacent South China Sea waters, days after Taiwan's coast guard warned off a Chinese coast guard vessel that approached the Taiwan-controlled atoll with its tracking system switched off; the statement followed Beijing's warning that Taiwan must "bear the consequences" for using a water cannon on a Chinese fishing boat near the islands.

beats.headline: Report: Israel had readied a post-midterm bombing campaign against Iran before Trump delayed it
beats.body: The Financial Times reported, citing three sources, that Israel had prepared a multi-day bombing campaign targeting Iran's nuclear sites, energy infrastructure and regime targets for the weekend of October 10, but Trump intervened to push any resumption of strikes until after the November 3 US midterms; a source told the FT restarting the operation in the coming weeks would not be unreasonable, and Israel's military reportedly warned that renewed fighting could force a delay of Israel's own October 27 election.

beats.headline: Anthropic's Claude Duet agent reaches Pro and Max subscribers via waitlist
beats.body: Anthropic's Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that can send daily briefs, track connected apps and handle tasks like scheduling and financial forecasts, is rolling out as a research preview on iOS, Android and the web to Pro and Max subscribers through a waitlist; TechCrunch frames it as Anthropic's answer to Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, and Anthropic says it will ask for approval before major actions like sending payments.

beats.headline: Bears TE Cole Kmet carted off with knee injury against Patriots
beats.body: Cole Kmet left Thursday night's game against New England on a cart after a hard fourth-quarter hit to his right knee; the severity wasn't immediately known, and the Bears are expected to give an update on his status in the coming days.
